                  is a business entity, or some person who has an operator's license and who is responsible
                  for the acts of all persons serving any alcoholic beverages to customers. For the
                  purpose of this article, any member of the licensee's or permittee's immediate family

questions.prompt: Can you drink alcohol in Avoca's village park?
choices: Yes, except between 1:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m.
questions.answer: Yes, except between 1:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m.
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 18. State Law reference— Municipal regulation of alcohol beverages, Wis. Stats. § 125.10.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Legal drinking age means 21 years of age. Underage person means a person who has not attained the legal drinking age. (Code 1982, § 10.01(2a)) Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2 . State Law reference— Similar definitions, Wis. Stats. § 125.02.

(a) Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, the drinking of any intoxicating
               liquors or fermented malt beverages, or the carrying of an open container which contains
               an intoxicating liquor or fermented malt beverage is prohibited in the following places
               within the village: (1) On private property without the owner's consent. (2) On any street, roadway, alley, parking lot or sidewalk. (3) On any public property. (b) The prohibition of drinking intoxicating liquor and/or fermented malt beverages on
               any street, public place or other public area within the village as set forth in subsection
               (a) of this section shall not apply to the following: (1) Any organization enumerated in Wis. Stats. § 125.32(3m)(g) which has been issued a

questions.prompt: How is the village assessor chosen in Birchwood?

Appointed by a two-thirds vote of the Village Board
Appointed solely by the Village President

               order.

A CHARTER ORDINANCE RELATING TO THE APPOINTMENT OF A VILLAGE ASSESSOR. The Village Board of the Village of Birchwood does ordain as follows: SECTION 1. The Village of Birchwood, pursuant to sec. 61.195, and 66.01, Wis. Stats.,
            hereby elects not to be governed by portions of secs. 61.19, Wis. Stats. which are
            in conflict with this ordinance. SECTION 2. The elected office of Assessor is hereby abolished to be replaced by an
            appointed Assessor. Appointment shall be made by a ⅔ vote of the Village Board. SECTION 3. The appointed Assessor shall hold office for an indefinite term, subject
            to removal as provided in sec. 17.12 (1), (c) and (d), Wis. Stats. SECTION 4. The appointed Assessor shall perform all duties required by law, with compensation
            to be fixed by the Village Board. SECTION 5. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict herewith, are hereby
            replaced. SECTION 6. This is a charter ordinance and shall take effect 60 days after its passage
            and publication unless within such 60-day period, a referendum petition as provided
            by sec. 66.01, Wis. Stats., shall be filed, in which event the ordinance shall not
            take effect until it shall have been submitted to a referendum vote of electors and
            approved by a majority of electors voting thereon. Attest: Joan Fuller, Village Clerk E. Langosch, Village President Footnotes: --- ( 2 ) --- Editor's note— Printed herein is Charter Ordinance No. 43, adopted June 5, 1984.                up to not more than $10,000.00 or imprisoned for not more than nine months or both
               for each day that a violation is determined to exist. (5) Any person who gives away alcoholic beverages or using any other means to evade the
               laws relating to the sale of alcohol beverages may be penalized not less than $100.00
               and up to not more than $10,000.00 or imprisoned for not more than nine months or
               both for each day that a violation is determined to exist. (6) Any licensee who allows another person to use his or her license to sell alcohol beverages,

CHARTER ORDINANCE AMENDING CHARTER OF THE VILLAGE OF CAMERON WHEREAS, the Village of Cameron presently elects a village clerk and a village treasurer
            at an annual spring election in said village in odd-numbered years pursuant to Wisconsin
            Statutes 61.19 [Wis. Stats. § 61.19], and WHEREAS, the Village of Cameron desires to no longer have the offices of village clerk
            and village treasurer elected, and WHEREAS, the Village of Cameron desires to combine the offices of village clerk and
            village treasurer into a position of village clerk-treasurer and to have said office
            filled by appointment by the village board of the Village of Cameron, and WHEREAS, provision is made in Wisconsin Statutes 61.195, 61.197 and 66.01 [Wis. Stats.
            §§ 61.195, 61.197 and 66.01] for the Village of Cameron to accomplish this change; Now, let it therefore be resolved, that the Village of Cameron does hereby enact this
            Charter ordinance amending its village charter to discontinue the election of a village
            clerk and village treasurer effective at the end of their respective terms in the
            spring of 1971; that the village board does hereby abolish the offices of village
            clerk and village treasurer at the end of their present terms and does further create
            a new office of village clerk-treasurer, said office to be filled by appointment by
            the village board to serve for an indeterminate period at the pleasure of said village
            board effective the day following the end of the present terms of the elected village
            clerk and village treasurer, respectively; And let it further be resolved that this Charter ordinance is to be published as a
            Class 1 notice in the Rice Lake Chronotype under Chapter 985 of the Wisconsin Statutes
            [Wis. Stats. ch. 985] on the 27th day of January, 1971, to become effective sixty
           …

               provide the animal with proper shelter from sunlight and inclement weather. Proper
               shelter from sunlight shall require that when sunlight is likely to cause heat stress
               or exhaustion of an animal tied or caged outdoors, sufficient shade by natural or
               artificial means shall be provided to protect the animal from direct sunlight. Sufficient
               ventilation shall be provided to prevent any animal confined within a vehicle from
               suffering heat stress or exhaustion. If a dog or cat is tied or confined unattended
               outdoors under weather conditions which are likely to adversely affect the health
               of the animal, a shelter of suitable size to accommodate the animal shall be provided
               which is sufficient to protect the animal from such weather conditions. (Ord. of 3-8-1999, § I(12.04(11))

               waters of Crawford County will adversely affect the public health, safety, convenience,
               and general welfare and impair the tax base. The Legislature of Wisconsin has delegated
               responsibility to the counties to further the maintenance of safe and healthful conditions;

               pollution through: 1. Limiting structures to those areas where soil and geological conditions will provide
               a safe foundation. 2. Establishing minimum lot sizes to provide adequate area for private on-site waste
               treatment systems. 3. Controlling filling and grading to prevent soil erosion problems. 4. Limiting impervious surfaces to control runoff which carries pollutants. questions.prompt: In Elkhorn, certain convicted sex offenders generally may not live within how many feet of a school, public park, daycare, library, or playground?
questions.answer: 2,000 feet
questions.excerpt:
This chapter is a regulatory measure aimed at protecting the health and safety of
               children in Elkhorn from the risk that convicted sex offenders may reoffend in locations
               close to their residences. The City finds and declares that sex offenders are a serious
               threat to public safety. When convicted sex offenders reenter society, they are much
               more likely than any other type of offender to be re-arrested for a new rape or sexual
               assault. Given the high rate of recidivism for sex offenders and that reducing opportunity
               and temptation is important to minimizing the risk of re-offense, there is a need
               to protect children where they congregate or play in public places in addition to
               the protections afforded by state law near schools, day-care centers and other places
               children congregate or play at public parks. (Ord. No. 14-07, § 1, 2014.)

As used in this chapter and unless the context otherwise requires: (1) A "sexually violent offense" shall have the meaning as set forth in Section 980.01(6),
                  Wis. Stats., as amended from time to time. (2) A "crime against children" shall mean any of the following offenses set forth within
                  the Wisconsin Statutes, as amended, or the laws of this or any other state or the
                  federal government, having like elements necessary for conviction, respectively: (a) Section 940.225(1) First Degree Sexual Assault; (b) Section 940.225(2) Second Degree Sexual Assault; (c) Section 940.225(3) Third Degree Sexual Assault; (d) Section 940.22(2) Sexual Exploitation by Therapist; (e) Section 940.30 False Imprisonment-victim was minor and not the offender's child; (f) Section 940.31 Kidnapping-victim was minor and not the offender's child; (g) Section 944.01 Rape (prior statute); (h) Section 944.10 Sexual Intercourse with a Child (prior statute); (i) Section 944.06 Incest;…

(a) It is unlawful for any person to consume an alcohol beverage on any parking lot as
               defined in section 94-76 . (b) It is unlawful for any person to possess any bottle or receptacle containing alcohol
               beverages if the bottle or receptacle has been opened, the seal has been broken, or
               the contents of the bottle or receptacle have been partially removed on any parking
               lot as defined in section 94-76 . (c) Excluded from the provisions of this section are any parking lots that are licensed

No person shall erect, contrive, cause, continue, maintain or permit to exist any
               public nuisance within the City.

questions.answer: At least 2 feet
questions.excerpt:
(1) STATUTORY AUTHORIZATION. This ordinance is adopted pursuant to the authorization in
               §§ 61.35 and 62.23 and the requirements in § 87.30, Stats. (2) FINDING OF FACT. Uncontrolled development and use of the floodplains and rivers of
               this municipality would impair the public health, safety, convenience, general welfare,
               and tax base. (3) STATEMENT OF PURPOSE. This ordinance is intended to regulate floodplain development
               to: (a) Protect life, health and property; (b) Minimize expenditures of public funds for flood control projects; (c) Minimize rescue and relief efforts undertaken at the expense of the taxpayers; (d) Minimize business interruptions and other economic disruptions; (e) Minimize damage to public facilities in the floodplain; (f) Minimize the occurrence of future flood blight areas in the floodplain; (g) Discourage the victimization of unwary land and homebuyers; (h) Prevent increases in flood heights that could increase flood damage and result in
               conflicts between property owners; and (i) Discourage development in a floodplain if there is any practicable alternative to
               locate the activity, use or structure outside of the floodplain. (4) TITLE. This ordinance shall be known as the Floodplain Zoning Ordinance for the Village
               of Nashotah, Wisconsin. (5) GENERAL PROVISIONS. (a) AREAS TO BE REGULATED. This ordinance regulates all areas of special flood hazard
               identified as zones A, AO, AH, A1-30, or AE, on the Flood Insurance Rate Map. Additional
               areas identified on maps approved by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and
               Village of Nashotah may also be regulated under the provisions of this ordinance,
               where applicable. (b) OFFICIAL MAPS AND REVISIONS. Special Flood Hazard Areas (SFHA) are designated as zones
               A, A1-30, AE, AH, or AO on the Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs)…

questions.prompt: Who serves on Oakdale's park committee?
choices: One village board member and two resident members
questions.answer: One village board member and two resident members
questions.excerpt:
The village board finds that it would be beneficial to the village to establish the
               park committee. The main responsibilities of the committee would be to help prioritize
               what needs to be done in the park and what gets done to improve the park, search for
               grants, and communicate suggestions to the board regarding spending funds on the park. (Ord. No. 2023-03-01-A, § 1, 3-20-2023)

The park committee shall consist of one village board member and two resident members.
               The committee shall meet at the park (weather permitting), or at the village hall
               on even months of the year. Two members shall constitute a quorum. (Ord. No. 2023-03-01-A, § 2, 3-20-2023)

Committee members shall be appointed by the village board at the annual organizational
               meeting of the board, held on the third Monday in April. The resident committee members
               shall serve for a term of three years to be staggered to accommodate experience on
               the committee. Initially, one resident member will be appointed for a one-year term
               and one resident member for a three-year term with successive terms for three-year
               terms. The board member shall be appointed annually by the village board. The terms
               shall begin immediately upon appointment. (Ord. No. 2023-03-01-A, § 3, 3-20-2023)

               convenience and general welfare and impair the tax base. The Legislature of Wisconsin
               has delegated responsibility to all municipalities to: (a) Promote the public health, safety, convenience and general welfare. This chapter shall be known as, referred to, and cited as the "Outagamie County Agricultural

               referred to as this chapter. (Ord. No. E-2007-08, § 14.2, 5-22-2007)

(a) The County Board finds this chapter is designed to protect and promote the county's
               agricultural industry and also to protect and preserve the surface water, groundwater,
               and soil resources of the county, in order to protect the health, safety, and general
               welfare of the people and communities within the county. (b) The county permits operation of properly conducted agricultural operations within
               the county. Individuals purchasing or owning land located near agricultural lands
               of operation or included within an area zoned for agricultural purposes, may be subject
               to outcomes arising from such operations. Such outcomes may include, but are not limited
               to: noises, odors, lights, fumes, dust, smoke, insects, chemicals, operation of machinery
               (including aircraft) during a 24-hour period, storage and disposal of manure, and
               the application of chemical fertilizers, soil amendments, herbicides and pesticides.
               One or more of the outcomes described may occur as a result of any agricultural operation,
               which is in conformance with existing laws and regulations and accepted customs and
               standards. Individuals living near an agricultural area should be prepared to accept

(a) Purpose of section. In order to protect the parks, parkways, recreational facilities and conservancy areas
               within the village from injury, damage or desecration, these regulations are enacted. (b) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Park means all grounds, structures and watercourses which are or may be located within
               any area dedicated to the public use as a park, parkway, recreation facility, playground,
               swimming pool or conservancy area in the village. (c) Specific regulations. (1) Littering. No person shall litter, dump or deposit any rubbish, refuse, earth or other material

               first obtained from the village board, or designated committee thereof. (3) Bill posting. No person shall post, paste, fasten, paint or attach any placard, bill, notice, sign
               or advertising matter upon any structure, tree or other natural object in any park,
               except park regulations and other signs authorized by the village board or the public
               works and property committee. (4) Throwing stones and missiles. No person shall throw stones or other missiles in or into any park. (5) Removal of park equipment. No person shall erect, contrive, cause, continue, maintain or permit to exist any
               public nuisance within the Village.

A public nuisance is a thing, act, occupation, condition or use of property which
               continues for such length of time as to: (1) Substantially annoy, injure or endanger the comfort, health, repose or safety of the
               public. (2) In any way render the public insecure in life or in the use of property. (3) Greatly offend the public morals or decency. (4) Unlawfully and substantially interfere with, obstruct or tend to obstruct or render
               dangerous for passage any street, alley, highway, navigable body of water or other
               public way or the use of public property.

The following acts, omissions, places, conditions and things are specifically declared
               to be public health nuisances; but such enumeration shall not be construed to exclude
               other health nuisances coming within the definition of §10.02: (1) ADULTERATED FOOD. All decayed, adulterated or unwholesome food or drink sold or offered
               for sale to the public. (2) UNBURIED CARCASSES. Carcasses of animals, birds or fowl not intended for human consumption
               or food which are not buried or otherwise disposed of in a sanitary manner within
               24 hrs. after death. (3) BREEDING PLACES FOR INSECTS OR VERMIN. Accumulations of decayed animal or vegetable
               matter, trash, rubbish, rotting lumber, bedding, packing material, scrap metal or
               any material in which flies, mosquitoes, disease carrying insects, rats or other vermin
               can breed. (4) STAGNANT…

This chapter shall hereafter be known, cited and referred to as the "Town of Rib Mountain
               Refuse and Recycling Regulations".

Whereas it is the principal purpose of this chapter to promote the health, safety
               and welfare of Rib Mountain citizens, and whereas the Town determined that the collection
               of recyclables is an environmentally sound practice and an economically viable act,
               it is the intent of this chapter to encourage and achieve a successful recycling effort
               on the part of its citizens and suppliers of services. It is the further intent of
               this chapter to meet the requirements of Ch. 159, Wis. Stats. and Ch. NR 544, Wis.
               Adm. Code, pertaining to recycling of certain materials and the establishment of a
               timetable of bans for land filling and incineration. Whereas the Town does not operate
               its own landfill, the further intent of this chapter is to ensure the continued success
               of the Marathon County Ordinance pertaining to recycling and landfill use. Whereas,
               there are commercial handlers of refuse and recyclables, it is the further intent
               of this chapter to encourage the success of these haulers to further the cause of
               recycling in the Town.

               the county board of supervisors, the rules of this section shall be observed, unless
               such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the board. (b) Liberal construction. The provisions of this Code shall be liberally construed to affect the purposes expressed
               therein or implied from the expression thereof. In case of doubt or ambiguity in the
               meaning of such provisions, the general shall yield to the particular. Reference for
               interpretation and construction shall tend to further the accomplishment of the elimination
               of the particular purpose for which the provisions were enacted. Words shall be construed
               in their common and usual significance unless the contrary is clearly indicated. (c) Law. When the term "law" is used in this Code it includes applicable court decisions and

questions.prompt: Why does Sturgeon Bay protect shoreland wetlands?
choices: They store storm and flood water and filter sediments, nutrients, and other pollution that would otherwise drain into lakes and streams
They are kept mainly so more houses and parking lots can be built near the water
They exist only to raise the city’s tax base
They allow unlimited filling and excavation
questions.answer: They store storm and flood water and filter sediments, nutrients, and other pollution that would otherwise drain into lakes and streams
questions.excerpt:
(1) Statutory authorization. This chapter is adopted pursuant to the authorization in §§ 62.23, 62.231, 87.30
               and 144.26, Wis. Stats. (2) Finding of facts and purpose. Uncontrolled use of the shoreland-wetlands and pollution of the navigable waters
               of the city would adversely affect the public health, safety, convenience and general
               welfare and impair the tax base. The Legislature of Wisconsin has delegated responsibility
               to all municipalities to: (a) Promote the public health, safety, convenience and general welfare. (b) Maintain the storm and flood water storage capacity of wetlands. (c) Prevent and control water pollution by preserving wetlands which filter or store sediments,
               nutrients, heavy metals or organic compounds that would otherwise drain into navigable
               waters. (d) Protect fish, their spawning grounds, other aquatic life and wildlife by preserving
               wetlands and other aquatic habitat. (e) Prohibit certain uses detrimental to the shoreland-wetland area. (f) Preserve shore cover and natural beauty by restricting the removal of natural shoreland
               cover and controlling shoreland-wetland excavation, filling and other earth moving
               activities. (3) Title. This chapter may be cited as the Shoreland-Wetland Zoning Ordinance for Sturgeon
               Bay, Wisconsin. (Code 1992, § 19.01)

(1) Compliance. The use of wetlands and the alteration of wetlands within the shoreland area of the
               city shall be in full compliance with the terms of this chapter and other applicable
               local, state or federal regulations. (See section 19.08 of this chapter for the standards applicable to nonconforming uses.) All permitted
               development shall require the issuance of a zoning permit unless otherwise expressly
               excluded by a provision of this chapter. (2) Municipalities and state agencies…

Only if it is on a leash strong enough to hold it, held by someone able to control it
questions.answer: Only if it is on a leash strong enough to hold it, held by someone able to control it
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Animals, Wis. Stats. chs. 169—174.

Footnotes: --- ( 2 ) --- State Law reference— Dogs, Wis. Stats. ch. 174.

No owner of or person harboring or keeping a vicious dog or bitch in heat shall suffer
               the same to run outside an enclosure in which the dog shall be kept unless attached
               to a leash of sufficient strength to restrain the dog, held by a person competent
               to control the dog. For purposes of enforcing this section, a dog shall be deemed
               as being of a vicious disposition if, within any 12-month period, it bites a person
               or domestic animal two or more times, or inflicts serious injury to one person or
               one domestic animal in unprovoked circumstances off the owner's premises. (Code 2006, § 75-1; Ord. of 7-7-1986; Ord. No. 35-2016 , § 1, 2-4-2016)

               within the village on the public highways, alleys, grounds or parks, or off the premises
               of the owner or keeper of such dog, except in an agricultural district as defined
               by the village's zoning ordinance. A dog will be considered to be running at large
               if it is not under control of a person physically able to control it. (Code 2006, § 75-2; Ord. of 7-7-1986; Ord. No. 117-2023 , § 1, 11-9-2023)

questions.prompt: Who must build, repair, and pay the full cost of sidewalks along a Sun Prairie street?
questions.answer: The abutting property owner
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

A. It shall be the duty of the abutting owner to build, repair, construct and perpetually
               maintain sidewalks along or upon any street, alley or highway in the city and to pay
               the entire cost of construction thereof. Any owner of property fronting on any street
               for which a grade has been established may construct a sidewalk in front of such property,
               providing such sidewalk be built in conformity with the provisions of this section. B. Whenever the common council shall by resolution determine that a sidewalk be laid,
               rebuilt, repaired, lowered or raised along or upon any public street, alley or highway
               within the city, it shall proceed according to Section 66.615 and/or 66.22, Wisconsin
               Statutes. C. Sidewalks shall be located in such places as designated by the common council. No
               person shall remove any sidewalk without the permission of the director of public
               works. (Prior code § 6-2-2(a))

No person shall hereafter lay, remove, replace or repair any public sidewalk within
               the city unless he or she is under contract with the city to do such work or has obtained
               a permit therefor from the director of public works at least three days before work
               is proposed to be undertaken. No fee shall be charged for such permits and a bond
               shall not be required unless the value of such sidewalk work will exceed one thousand
               dollars ($1,000.00) as determined by the director of public works. Should the sidewalk
               work or other street fixtures disturbed by such sidewalk work become defective during
               the two years following the completion of such work, the city shall issue a notice
               to correct such defective work to the permittee (and the property owner, if different)
               in accordance with Section 12.04.040 . If the…

questions.prompt: In Superior, what may you not do to a bill or poster that a billposter had the right to put up?
choices: Paint over it after one week
Move it to a nearby pole
Cover it with a political flyer
questions.answer: Willfully deface or destroy it
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Buildings, construction and housing, ch. 34; licenses, permits and business regulations, ch. 74; planning, zoning and development, ch. 98; streets and sidewalks, ch. 106.

No person shall willfully deface or destroy any bill or poster, posted by a billposter
               upon any place where the billposter shall have the right to post the bill within the
               city. (Code 1971, § 3-1)

(a) It is the intention and purpose of this chapter to: (1) Promote the health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the city; (2) Promote the safety, convenience and enjoyment of public travel; (3) Preserve the natural beauty of the state and the city and any lands under its jurisdiction; (4) Aid in free flow of interstate commerce; (5) Conform to the express intent of national and state legislative bodies to control
               the erection and maintenance of outdoor advertising signs, displays and devices adjacent
               to the national system of interstate and defense highways; and (6) Promote the aesthetic advancement of the community and its natural and economic resources. (b) The provisions of this chapter shall be held to be the minimum requirements adopted
               to promote the health, safety, morals and general welfare of the city. It is not intended
               by this chapter to abrogate, impair, or interfere with any existing state or federal
               laws regulating outdoor advertising signs, displays and devices. Where, however, this
               chapter imposes a greater restriction upon the use of such signs, displays or devices
               than such state or federal laws, the provisions of this chapter shall govern to the
               extent permitted by such laws. (c) It is declared that it is in the public interest to control the erection, maintenance
               and supervision of outdoor advertising signs, displays and devices adjacent to state
               and federal…

                  facilities will be considered vandalism. E. Dogs are allowed on recreational trails designated by the city council by resolution,

(a) Statutes Adopted. Except as otherwise specifically provided in this Code, the statutory provisions
               in Chapters 110, 194, and 340 through 349 of the Wisconsin Statutes, describing and
               defining regulations with respect to vehicles and traffic, for which the penalty is
               a forfeiture only, exclusive of any regulations for which the statutory penalty is
               a fine or term of imprisonment or exclusively state charges, are hereby adopted and
               by reference made a part of this Chapter as if fully set forth herein. The statutory
               sections listed shall be designated as part of this Code by adding the prefix "10-1-"
               to each statute section number. Any act required to be performed or prohibited by
               any regulation incorporated herein by reference is required or prohibited by this
               Chapter. Any future amendments, revisions or modifications of the statutory regulations
               in Chapters 340 through 349 incorporated herein are intended to be made part of this
